headline: Tk 180cr illicit assets: ACC approves charge sheet against Anisul Huq and 3 others
summary: The former law minister and his associates are accused of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income and conducting suspicious bank transactions totaling Tk 737.24 crore.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against former law minister Anisul Huq and three of his associates for allegedly acquiring Tk 180.86 crore in illicit assets.
The probe found that while Anisul's legitimate income was Tk 13.28 crore, he accumulated assets worth Tk 172.24 crore beyond his known sources of income.
The charge sheet also includes three relatives: Mohammad Iqbal, Sheikh Md Iftekharul Islam, and Jebunnesa Begum Huq, who allegedly held assets in their names on behalf of the former minister.
Investigation reveals that the three relatives held movable assets totaling Tk 84.05 crore, including significant shares in Citizens Bank.
The ACC also uncovered suspicious transactions totaling Tk 737.24 crore across 23 bank accounts linked to Anisul Huq and his interests.
The charge sheet was approved under laws including the ACC Act 2004, the Penal Code, the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012.
Anisul Huq was arrested on August 13, 2024, from the Sadarghat area of Dhaka while allegedly attempting to flee the country by waterway and has remained in custody since.
caption:
Tk 180.86 crore in illicit assets and Tk 737.24 crore in suspicious transactions. The ACC has moved against former law minister Anisul Huq.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against former law minister Anisul Huq and three of his associates for allegedly acquiring Tk 180.86 crore in illicit assets.

The probe found that while Anisul's legitimate income was Tk 13.28 crore, he accumulated assets worth Tk 172.24 crore beyond his known sources of income.

The charge sheet also includes three relatives: Mohammad Iqbal, Sheikh Md Iftekharul Islam, and Jebunnesa Begum Huq, who allegedly held assets in their names on behalf of the former minister.

Investigation reveals that the three relatives held movable assets totaling Tk 84.05 crore, including significant shares in Citizens Bank.

The ACC also uncovered suspicious transactions totaling Tk 737.24 crore across 23 bank accounts linked to Anisul Huq and his interests.

The charge sheet was approved under laws including the ACC Act 2004, the Penal Code, the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012.

Anisul Huq was arrested on August 13, 2024, from the Sadarghat area of Dhaka while allegedly attempting to flee the country by waterway and has remained in custody since.

headline_marked: 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours: [[Dengue cases surge in September]]
headline: 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours: Dengue cases surge in September
summary: September's infection rate has already surpassed August's total, with 7 deaths reported in the last 24 hours alone.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 1,753 patients were hospitalized in the last 24 hours, marking the highest single-day admission record for this year.
The surge is alarming; by Wednesday, the number of dengue infections in September has already exceeded the total number of cases recorded in August (21,070 vs 20,536).

Seven people died from the virus in the last 24 hours. All seven victims were from outside Dhaka city, with three from the Khulna division and others from Chattogram, Mymensingh, Rangpur, and Rajshahi divisions.
Death tolls for September have already surpassed August's records, with 74 deaths recorded this month compared to 54 in August.
Since the beginning of the year, a total of 56,916 people have been infected with dengue in Bangladesh.
Entomologist Professor Kabirul Bashar of Jahangirnagar University warned that cases could exceed 30,000 this month due to negligence in prevention efforts.
While the government has launched new initiatives to control the virus, experts emphasize that these must be implemented effectively on the ground rather than just for media coverage.
